Exercise A

Read & Spot

Read the text and choose the correct future form for each gap.

Before you read

This question is not marked - just write what comes to mind.

Lea's Saturday

How it works: a plan takes going to — "Lea is going to visit her aunt." A fixed arrangement takes the present progressive — "She is meeting Ben at ten." A spontaneous decision takes will — "I'll help you!"

1 In the morning she her aunt in hospital — she planned it weeks ago.

2 At ten o'clock she Ben at the bus stop — that is fixed.

3 "I carry your bags for you," she tells her aunt — a spontaneous offer.

4 In the afternoon Lea and Ben a barbecue in the park — everything is arranged.

5 Ben has forgotten the drinks, so Lea says: "No problem, I get some from the shop."

6 Look at those black clouds — it rain later!

Exercise B

will or going to?

Eight decisions: plan or prediction with evidence (going to) — or spontaneous decision, promise and guess (will)?

Task

1 Look at that little boy on the wall! He fall.

2 A: I have decided. B: Really? A: Yes, I study medicine.

3 A: The phone is ringing. B: I get it!

4 We have bought the tickets — we fly to Rome in July.

5 I promise I never lie to you again.

6 She has saved enough money — she buy the guitar next week.

7 Don't worry about the mess — I help you clean up.

8 Watch out! You drop your phone!

Exercise C

Arrangements & Timetables

The present progressive talks about fixed arrangements — and the present simple about timetables.

Task

1 The train at 9.15 every morning.

2 We dinner with Grandma on Sunday — it is all arranged.

3 The concert at 8 pm — it says so on the ticket.

4 I my driving test on Friday — the appointment is fixed.

5 The school holidays on 25 June.

6 A: I can't open the window. B: I help you?

Exercise D

Writing

Write about your plans for next weekend.

Task

Your English partner school wants to know what a typical weekend looks like for you. Write a short text (6-8 sentences) about next weekend: use going to for two plans, the present progressive for two fixed arrangements, and will for at least one promise or spontaneous decision.
